item.title: The Millionaire Who Filmed The Evidence Against Himself
item.description: The search for Lucie Blackman led police to videos documenting Japanese property developer Joji Obara’s assaults on women. In 2007, he was sentenced to life for raping nine women and causing Carita Ridgway’s death. Japan’s Supreme Court upheld his sentence in 2010.

item.title: Her Foster Father Recruited Her To Kill His Wife
item.description: Sabrina Zunich was 18 when she killed her foster mother, Lisa Knoefel, in Ohio in 2012. She later testified that her foster father, Kevin, had planned the murder. Zunich pleaded guilty to aggravated murder; Kevin was convicted of complicity in the killing. Both received life sentences in 2014.

item.title: Her Story Changed When Police Heard The Neighbor’s Camera
item.description: Cosplay model Melissa Turner initially said she remembered little about the night her fiancé, Matthew Trussler, died in Florida in 2019. A neighbor’s security recording challenged her account. A jury rejected her self-defense claim, convicting her of second-degree murder in 2022. She received 20½ years in prison.

item.title: He Invented A Secret Organization To Keep Her Captive
item.description: Cameron Hooker held Colleen Stan captive in California from 1977 to 1984, claiming a secret group called “The Company” would harm her family if she escaped. His wife exposed the lie and helped Stan leave. Hooker was convicted of kidnapping and sexual assaults in 1985 and sentenced to 104 years.

item.title: She Survived Long Enough To Name Her Six Attackers
item.description: After a week in captivity in Manchester, 16-year-old Suzanne Capper reached help and identified her six attackers. She died from her injuries four days later, in December 1992. Four people were convicted of her murder the following year.

item.title: Phil Spector’s Chauffeur Heard More Than A Gunshot
item.description: After actress Lana Clarkson was killed at Phil Spector’s home in 2003, his chauffeur testified that the music producer emerged holding a gun and said, “I think I killed somebody.” Convicted of second-degree murder in 2009, Spector received 19 years to life and died in custody in 2021.
